newsitem.title: USA: Penn Octane to supply Mexico City buses.
newsitem.headline: Penn Octane to supply Mexico City buses.

text.p: Penn Octane Corp said it agreed with the private owners of Mexico City's transportation system to provide up to 1,500 new buses and 1,000 converted taxis for exclusive use of compressed natural gas at CNG stations to be owned and operated by Penn Octane.

The agreement is subject to a number of conditions including financing arrangements satisfactory to Mexican companies, and the financing and construction of a minimum of four CNG stations by Penn Octane.

The buses will be purchased, at a cost seen approaching $90 million, through the recently announced Dina dealership acquired by Penn Octane. The company said it will be entitled to a dealer's commission based on the purchase price, and Penn Octane expects to convert the taxis from gasoline to CNG.

The agreement is with Servicios Metropolitanos De Transporte 17 de Marzo SA de CV, Autotransportes Urbanos Siglo Nuevo SA de CV and Sistema De Transportes En Taxis SA de CV collectively known as Servicios.
As part of the agreement, Servicios has entered into a long term fuel purchase commitment pursuant to which its vehicles will use CNG purchased from stations owned by Penn Octane, the company said.
